text:
sara: Quick follow-up from the morning sync — I'm sketching an alternative admission strategy for dedicated GPU pools that trades short-lived credits for a tiny time-window reservation. Wanted to get thoughts before I bake an RFC.
ajay: can you outline the main problem we're solving vs existing credit/headroom approaches?
sara: Sure. Right now we use token-like credits (reserve X tokens per tenant) + a long tail headroom bucket. That works but: 1) small bursty workloads either consume tokens too quickly, 2) long idle-to-burst transitions cause aggressive prewarm which spikes cost, and 3) accounting across shards is messy.
leo: sounds familiar. What's the new idea?
sara: The idea: instead of handing units that represent compute, hand short-duration "time-window reservations" (TWR). Reservation example: 30s window with guaranteed N concurrent slots. Tenants acquire windows, not tokens. Windows expire automatically, so we avoid dangling credits. Windows can be stacked for longer sustained runs.
jenna: interesting. How do you handle the warmup cost? If a tenant bursts and we prewarm per-window, won't we still pay a lot for GPU spin-up?
sara: Two mitigations: 1) allow window prewarm coalescing — if multiple windows are requested within a small jitter window, treat as same prewarm event; 2) have an operator-level soft-lease that can be promoted from a TWR to a persistent lease when a tenant exceeds a threshold. Promotion happens with hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.
ajay: what's the admission logic? priority, fairness, cost-awareness?
sara: Admission priorities: SLA tier > realtime priority > cost band. But we also introduce a small probabilistic thinning for best-effort when headroom is tight: best-effort windows may be admitted with p < 1 to smooth tail pressure.
leo: can you show a sketch of the admission check? even pseudo config helps.
sara: pasted quick config snippet:
```
admission:
  window_size: 30s
  slots_per_window: 4
  prewarm_coalesce_ms: 200
  promotion_threshold: 3_windows_in_60s
  thinning:
    best_effort_prob: 0.6
    cooldown_ms: 1000
```
jenna: I like the coalescing param. But what about cross-shard coordination? windows live on shard A but traffic can be routed to B.
sara: We keep windows federated: a tenant can hold windows on multiple shards, but the global operator maintains a cheap lease-index (compact counters) so promotions and global quota checks are approximate but monotonic. The idea is eventual correctness with safety limits.
ajay: how do we account cost/chargeback? tokens were easy to bill.
sara: Windows map to billable seconds. Each acquired window increments a tenant's usage meter by window_size * slots_used. For promoted leases we backfill using the actual runtime recorded. So billing stays accurate enough for end-of-month reports.
leo: any SLO impact modelling?
sara: Early sim shows median tail latency improves for bursty traffic because windows are pre-bound and avoid queue-to-warm cycles. But p95 might worsen for churn if coalescing is too aggressive — that's tunable.
jenna: What about retry/backoff client-side? do we expect clients to retry aggressively and starve best-effort windows?
sara: We'll expose a transient-retry hint in 429 responses: `Retry-After: window-backoff-ms`. Clients using our SDK can use exponential backoff keyed by tenant-token to avoid global thundering.
autoscaler-bot: scale-decision: observed 18% increase in prewarm events in last 10m; recommending increase prewarm_coalesce_ms to 350ms for test buckets.
ajay: nice signal. For the RFC, can we include an operator handoff section: how the admin shrinks windows during emergencies, and a rollback plan?
sara: Yep — plan draft: 1) operator can reduce window_size or slots_per_window, 2) enable strict serial admission (no thinning), 3) throttle promotions. Rollback: revert config, let windows expire (~30s) and drain.
leo: sounds good. One more: how do we test without affecting prod tenants?
sara: test harness idea: shadow admission in prod with canary tenants (tagged) and synthetic bursts. We'll run for 24h and compare cold starts, cost-per-token, and p99 tail.
jenna: +1. Also add monitoring dashboards: windows-in-flight, promotions/sec, prewarm-coalesces, thinning-rejects.
ajay: ok i'm convinced this is worth an RFC. Sara, want me to pair on the cost model section?
sara: please — that'd be great. I'll draft RFC this week and ping for review.
leo: ping me for the simulation config.
jenna: thanks sara, looking forward to it :tada:
sara: thanks all! will share link when drafted.
